subject: Next 6-week MAP sprint: legal gating, procurement handoffs & parallel orderform lanes
messages:
From: Ciara Nolan <ciara.nolan@medivex.com>

Cc: contracts@medivex.com
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & evaluation timeline questions

Jonas —

Thanks for the call earlier. Per our procurement team, we need a concrete MAP that makes sequencing explicit for legal (MSA/DPA) vs procurement (order form). Two constraints: (1) our legal needs 10 business days for DPA review if no redlines, and (2) procurement requires evidence of SOC 2 scope and retention windows before final PO release.

Can you share a 4–6 week sprint plan that shows which signatures can be parallelized (we prefer to sign order form once MSA is in executed state, but could accept a contingent order form signature with payment terms blocked). Also please include who at Redwood will own the DocuSign and who will chase the procurement SOW.

Thanks —
Ciara
Sr. Procurement Manager, MediVex

Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next 6-week MAP sprint: legal gating, procurement handoffs & parallel orderform lanes

Ciara —

Appreciate the clarity. Draft MAP attached (MVX-MAP-v1.xlsx) and a short sequencing note below. I tried to prioritize parallel workstreams so procurement can prepare PO while legal completes review. High level:

- Week 0 (today): Redwood shares MAP + SOC2 summary (attached). Redwood legal: Laura Bennett will own DPA loop; Sales (me) will own order-form DocuSign flow.
- Weeks 1–2: Legal review window for MSA (target 5 business days); DPA routed in parallel but may need the 10 business days you noted for deeper review.
- Week 2: Procurement receives final order form draft; procurement team to start internal PO approval in parallel with DPA review.
- Week 3–4: If MSA executed, we relax order form payment terms and can move to DocuSign. If MSA is delayed, we can sign a conditional order form (signature + payment block) and convert post-execution.
- Week 5–6: Target cutover and onboarding kickoff; contingency: if DPA needs >10 bd, push onboarding but allow technical ramp with sandbox access under NDA.

Action owners (quick):
- Laura Bennett (laura_bennett@redwood.com): DPA redline intake + SOC2 evidence handoff.
- Jonas Weber (me): Order form coordination, DocuSign initiation, HubSpot deal updates.
- Karthik Iyer (karthik_iyer@redwood.com): Pricing confirmation for dedicated capacity lanes and one-off billing terms.

I attached the MAP spreadsheet with milestone dates populated for a 6-week lane and a condensed 4-week aggressive lane. Please review and call out any fixed procurement milestone that would block signature. If that looks reasonable, I'll turn the order form into a DocuSign envelope with conditional fields (payment_hold = true) and route to your contracts address.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
attachments: MVX-MAP-v1.xlsx, SOC2-summary-2025.pdf

Thanks Jonas / Ciara — quick legal notes as we align the MAP:

1) DPA scope: we'll need to align on subprocessors and data flows; suggest a 2-day working session between Redwood Security and MediVex InfoSec the week after next.
2) Timebox: Laura confirms we can target 5 business days for MSA if the customer applies minor redlines only. For DPA please assume 10 business days baseline unless we get a pre-approved DPA template from your side.
3) Evidence: SOC2-summary-2025.pdf should be placed into your procurement packet (Jonas: please confirm the link we share to procurement). If MediVex procurement requires an attestation letter, allow 2 additional bd for legal sign-off.

Recommendation: proceed with Jonas' conditional order form approach. We will mark the DPA and MSA as parallel tasks but MSA execution unlocks payment term relaxation.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Looping in a short pricing note — MediVex asked about a dedicated-capacity lane for initial 3-month pilot. Two items to confirm:

1) If procurement signs conditional order form (payment blocked) and subsequently completes PO post-MSA, we need a one-time invoice trigger or credit memo flow. We can support either; recommend credit memo as it's easier for finance.
2) If MediVex requests 99th percentile latency SLA higher than standard, that needs a dedicated SLA appendix and may add ~12% to committed capacity price.

Jonas: when you create the DocuSign, include optional fields for (a) credit memo flag, (b) SLA appendix opt-in. That helps procurement and speeds AR.

—Karthik
Director, Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
